title: The one-night step and being a late starter
summary: He got the step by luck after long practice; he calls himself a late starter still working toward perfection.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: What was that step that you were trying to get that night?
You stayed up all night just to --
All night, yeh, just to get that step.

I got it one night by luck. I'd been practicing all along. I'd do it in the daytime, but I couldn't get it finished in the daytime, so I'd go through the night. But I didn't stop doing it until I got it and it went to the next morning.
So you were really a late starter when it came to tap dancing.

Yeah, I'm the last one. I'm the last one that's considered, you know what I mean? There were a lot of dancers, but no one had reached the penacle like Bill Robinson, Fred Astaire and all them, understand? They're still trying to get there. But I'm working on mine until perfection. I've had consideration in the -- what is that paper -- Ebony -- another one called -- it's a woman's magazine, I can't think of the name of it.
